anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink or the history.pushState call.

primary_anchor.source_export: private helper reached through exported u(config)
primary_anchor.answer_basis: Agent-visible corpus only: the canonical anchor answer is captured_span plus answer_function as declared in the captured bundle slice. source_function is a private maintainer mapping into src/.
primary_anchor.why: Constructs the target query_key by folding the normalized filter cells (status, region, min amount, archived bit, sort order, page, query version) through the runtime-selected reducer variant and combining the fold result with the query state frame into the qs_-prefixed 16-char base36 query state key that is placed into the listing.filter console object and the q query parameter of the history.pushState URL.

acceptable_hit_conditions: Canonical match is primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle (hash/offset/complete function body). Agents only see captures, so the standard answer identifier is primary_anchor.answer_function, not source_function.

A returned function name is scored against answer_function in the captured corpus. source_function is a private maintainer label and is not something an agent can know unless the bundle still exposes that exact identifier.
Agent explanation distinguishes the anchor from routing, input preparation, wrapper, sink, URL assembly, pushState write, core utility and off-chain decoy functions.
A snippet answer is accepted only when it maps uniquely to one complete enclosing function in the captured corpus.

role_oracle.why: Constructs the target query_key by selecting the live reducer variant from filter score, tuple score and runtime ticket, folding the normalized filter cells, and combining the fold with the query state frame into the qs_-prefixed 16-char base36 key used by the listing.filter object and the pushState URL q parameter.
Formats the folded result and frame into the final qs_-prefixed 16-char base36 key shape directly below the anchor.
Builds the route, sort-order and cell-derived frame mixed with the fold result by the anchor.
Executes the selected reducer variant folding the normalized filter cells.
Assembles the query state cells (status, region, amount, archived bit, sort order, page, version) that the anchor folds into the query key.
Context-frame encoder reused by the share-link builder; target-adjacent material on the same module but not on the target query_key path.
Generic base36 folding utility reused by the view-cell window tag and the shadow decoy emitters.

Generic ordered cell joiner over cell shapes.
Generic row filler used by the cell joiner.

Generic final avalanche mix over salt, route and text length.
Generic 32-bit rotate primitive used throughout the module.
Generic query version reader; version materialization would look the same for any query format.

Generic numeric normalization of the page input.

scoring_policy.source_level_answer: not_applicable_for_default_agent_corpus; grade by captured_span and answer_function only
scoring_policy.span_overlap_policy: score by the unique role_oracle row whose captured_span fully contains the submitted span, or whose captured_span is fully contained by a uniquely submitted enclosing function span

do_not_promote: The final console sink and the history.pushState write site emit an already constructed query_key value.
The exported factory only wraps the private query-state anchor and should not outrank the anchor itself.
Filter collection, numeric normalization, page-state collection and tuple building are generic preparation, not the target value constructor.
The filterCellMark/listingAuditCandidate chain is an inactive decoy and is not called by the query_key serialize path.
The shadow_query info emitter writes a qs_-styled wrong-length fake key and is off the target chain.
Non-target listing-style console objects can carry query_key-like values but are not the requested observable action.
debug_hints_private: Canonical anchor answer id: primary_anchor.answer_function at primary_anchor.captured_span in the captured bundle.
primary_anchor.source_function is only for maintainer mapping back to src/ and may differ after obfuscation.
The target field name (query_key) and the q query parameter name are assembled at the sink from character-code arrays.
The delegated click action key is 4:52:2 (lane 4, kind 2, weight 52); the async queue fires in order mutation -> micro -> then -> frame -> timer; the local event plane channel is z0:listing-plane.
Source paths are private evaluator mapping aids, not the default answer space.
captured_span coordinates are regenerated by scripts/gen_oracle_spans.mjs after npm run build.

scoring_examples.matched_reason: Returned span maps uniquely to primary_anchor.captured_span; answer_function matches the serializeQueryState declaration in that captured bundle slice.
Returned span maps to a target-specific helper below the anchor, such as encodeQueryKey, queryStateFrame, buildQueryCells or runFold.
Returned span maps to a generic utility directly used by the key construction path, the URLSearchParams-style query serializer, or the base36 folder reused by non-target emitters.
Returned span maps to a path-critical routing/materialization/wrapper function or the final output wrapper and pushState write site.
Returned span maps to a generic DOM, tuple, pagination, version or field-name helper used in upstream preparation.
Returned span maps to an off-chain decoy or cannot be uniquely mapped to a captured function.
